summary: Backend regression and targeted auth checks passed; desktop UI core flows passed, while client catalog verification exposed a test-selection ambiguity and CORS preflight rejected the configured public origin.

critical.issue: OPTIONS request from FRONTEND_URL returns 400 Disallowed CORS origin and no access-control-allow-origin header, despite allow_credentials=true and explicit FRONTEND_URL configuration.

action_items: Fix runtime CORS origin loading/matching so the configured frontend origin is accepted for credentialed preflight requests.
Retest client catalog after explicitly selecting the newly created store; the interrupted check selected the first pre-existing store, not the newly created one.
critical_code_review_comments: CORS configuration appears correct in source but is not active at runtime; verify deployed environment values and process reload.
seed_data_creation: Created TEST-prefixed API records and UI Store ui2 with client ui-ui2@example.com and product UI Burger; no seeded records modified.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Health, cookie auth/me/logout, dashboard, plans, store creation, client isolation API, catalog API, unconfigured WAHA, lockout (401 x5 then 429), and desktop/mobile login passed. CORS preflight needs retest. UI WAHA notice was not conclusively asserted because the existing notice selector was reused before async completion.
rca of the issue: Source builds origins from CORS_ORIGINS and FRONTEND_URL, but live OPTIONS responses say Disallowed CORS origin and omit allow-origin. Likely runtime environment parsing or stale process configuration; inspect effective process env and supervisor reload. Client catalog finding was caused by selectedStore defaulting to stores[0] after creation, so the browser test did not select the new store before checking its product.
